Subject: Reserve SLA binding: Acme Health pilot — carve + autoscale exception

Team —

Quick context: Acme Health (pilot customer) has finished legal and procurement signoff pending a short operations binding: they want a 4-week guaranteed dedicated slice (30% of a p4d pool equivalent) for their clinical inference pilot starting Nov 3. Procurement attached an MOU that references a 99.5% availability SLAs and a clause asking for an autoscale grace (they will run steady but have occasional burst analysis that could exceed our default autoscale thresholds).

Ask: can Infra (Jonas) provide a temporary reservation carve (30% equivalent) + an autoscale policy exception (raise burst tolerance and allow scheduled warm-up windows) for Nov 3 — Nov 30? Product (Kim) — we need your confirmation that the pilot's expected latency/seq-length distribution matches the reserved profile or we risk degraded p99s. Sales (Marcus) — customer is sensitive to calendar timing; if we miss Nov 3 they’re likely to delay and bring competing vendors into the evaluation.

Attachments: Acme_MOU_v1.pdf, capacity_matrix.xlsx (high-level usage numbers from Acme).

Primary constraints I know about: we are in a high utilization window in nov due to Q4 pilots; autoscale policies are strict unless an exemption is approved by infra/product.

Proposed timeline:
- Today: confirm feasibility and carve size
- 10/13: signed MOU inbound (procurement)
- 10/20: operations prep and canary run in staging
- 11/03: pilot go-live

Can each of you reply with feasibility and any blocking risks? If Jonas cannot commit, please explain operational alternatives (pre-warm, fallback to hosted model with tighter cost share, etc.).

Thanks — Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Success (Commercial)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Reserve SLA binding: Acme Health pilot — carve + autoscale exception

Thanks for the context, Evelyn.

From a Product perspective: the matrix shows Acme is planning 1.2k concurrent inference sessions during peak windows with average sequence lengths ~1.5k tokens (prompts + clinical reports). That profile is heavier than our typical PLG pilots but still within what the p4d slices can handle if we tune batching and KV cache TTL aggressively. Important notes:

- If we grant an autoscale exception that allows sustained higher concurrency, we need a short canary window (2–4 hours) in staging to validate p99 latency is within the 300–500ms target for their LLM variant.
- We must version-pin the model (no auto-upgrades) for the duration of the reservation to avoid an unintended perf regression during the pilot.
- Product recommends a slightly larger carve (35% equivalent) for the first week to absorb warm-up noise; we can step down to 30% if metrics settle.

Blocking items:
1) Does Infra have the capacity headroom to hold 35% for the week of Nov 3?
2) Can the reservation include an automated fallback route to a compatible, lower-cost model variant if p99 breaches for >15 minutes? (This would keep the customer online while we investigate.)

If Infra confirms headroom, Product will schedule the canary and prepare a model pin/rollout plan (we'll need the exact model id from Acme).

Kim
Kimberly Park
Product Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Reserve SLA binding: Acme Health pilot — carve + autoscale exception

TL;DR: We can support a time-boxed carve + autoscale policy exception with conditions.

Details / constraints:
- Current projection for the p4d pool in us-west for the Nov window shows ~82% committed utilization across reserved accounts. We have limited flexible headroom but can re-slice some short-lived experimental slots.
- We can offer a staged carve: 35% equivalent for Nov 3–Nov 9 (warm-up & canary), then step down to 30% for Nov 10–Nov 30. That matches Product's ask.
- Autoscale exception: we can raise the burst tolerance to +40% of the slice for scheduled windows, but only if the customer agrees to a strict pre-declared burst schedule and pays for the overage at a committed burst rate. Otherwise we allow a one-off 30-minute emergency burst with automatic throttling after that.

Operational requirements we need from Acme (and from Product/Sales to collect):
1) Exact model id and container image checksum (for pinning).
2) Two-hour canary window dates (we prefer Nov 28–29 lower-run would be tough; aim for Oct 29).
3) Signed MOU acknowledging overage pricing and fallback behavior.

Fallback options if we cannot hold the carve at any point:
- Immediate redirect to a hosted variant (slightly higher latency but preserves uptime)
- Queue-based graceful degradation with pre-warned error-codes to the customer app

I'll need a formal ops ticket to reserve the slice (INFRA-4720) and sign-off from Product on the model pin + canary plan. Marcus, if Procurement is pushing a hard SLA clause we should get explicit sign-off on overage charges — otherwise legal will push back on our side for exposure.

I'll provision a tentative carve as soon as INFRA-4720 is created and the MOU is signed.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference
